title: European Commission says a publicly available AI tool was used in a cyber campaign that took HR systems offline
date_note: Day the Commission spokesperson publicly commented, per Euronews (published that day); Euronews gives 22 October as the day the attack was detected.
summary: Euronews reports that Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier said the attack used a publicly available AI tool and was first detected and confirmed on 22 October. The HR platform Sysper was inaccessible for several days and several internal apps were taken offline as a precaution. Regnier said the Commission has not detected evidence of a data breach affecting staff as a whole; the investigation is ongoing and no one has been named as responsible.
plain: The European Commission says a publicly available AI tool was used against it. HR systems were offline for several days. It says it has found no evidence that all staff data was breached; the investigation continues.
exec: The Commission says staff HR systems were disrupted; it has not named an attacker and says it found no evidence of a staff-wide data breach.

validation.note: Euronews, The Register and Egovernment (dpa) each report the Commission's confirmation of an AI-assisted cyber campaign; Euronews quotes the spokesperson directly.
